headline: RBI: UNSC ISIL & Al-Qaida Sanctions List amended for one entry; UAPA s.51A compliance
summary_points: RBI has circulated the UNSC amendment to one entry (QDi.198) on the ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaida Sanctions List, as informed by the MEA.
The amendment was enacted per UNSC press release SC/16515 under resolutions 1267 (1999), 1989 (2011) and 2253 (2015).
Regulated entities must act under Chapter IX of the RBI KYC Directions, 2025 and follow the UAPA Order dated February 2, 2021 (amended April 22, 2024).
De-listing requests received by a bank are to be forwarded electronically to the Joint Secretary (CTCR), MHA.
Entities must take note of the UNSC communication and ensure meticulous compliance.
who_is_affected: Commercial banks, SFBs, payment banks, co-operative banks, RRBs, LABs, NBFCs, ARCs and All India Financial Institutions.
action_required: Update sanctions screening with the amended entry, check that no accounts exist in the listed name, and follow the UAPA Order procedure under Chapter IX of the KYC Directions.

social.linkedin:
RBI has issued a circular on implementing Section 51A of the UAPA, 1967, following an update to the UNSC's ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaida Sanctions List.

Key points:

- One entry (QDi.198) on the list has been amended, as per UNSC press release SC/16515 communicated by the MEA.
- Regulated entities must act under Chapter IX of the RBI KYC Directions, 2025 and follow the UAPA Order of February 2, 2021 (amended April 22, 2024).
- Any de-listing request received by a bank is to be forwarded electronically to the Joint Secretary (CTCR), MHA.

The circular applies to banks, NBFCs, ARCs and All India Financial Institutions. Compliance teams should refresh their sanctions screening databases and confirm there are no accounts in the name of the listed person.

Circular reference: RBI/2026-27/309 dated November 26, 2026.

Please verify the details with the official RBI source before acting.
